rules: Output Directory: All final, deployable static assets (e.g., `index.html`, `style.css`, `script.js`) MUST be placed into a `dist/` directory at the project root.
Source Files: For simple projects, source files SHOULD be placed directly in the `dist/` directory. There is no separate `src/` directory or build step required.
Core Technologies: The project MUST use only standard HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript.

No Frameworks: The project is strictly FORBIDDEN from using any JavaScript frameworks (like React, Vue, Svelte) or CSS frameworks (like Bootstrap) unless explicitly requested and approved as part of a project type change.
Dependencies: The project should have no `package.json` or `node_modules`. All code must be self-contained.
Static Hosting: The infrastructure plan for a 'simple' project type will always target a static hosting solution, such as a Google Cloud Storage bucket configured for website hosting.
CI/CD Workflow ONLY: The deployment plan MUST consist of a single GitHub Actions workflow file (e.g., `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`).
FORBIDDEN: The plan is strictly FORBIDDEN from including a separate `deploy.sh` or any other deployment script. All deployment logic MUST be contained within the CI/CD workflow file.
Deployment Logic: The CI/CD workflow MUST be configured to deploy ONLY the contents of the `dist/` directory (e.g., by using `gsutil rsync -r dist/ gs://<bucket-name>`).
